project.title: The 400-year-old shark
fact_sources: Nielsen et al. 2016, Science 353:702, eye-lens radiocarbon dating of Greenland sharks (392 +/- 120 yr; 95% range 272-512)

script: Scientists dated this shark to three hundred and ninety two years old. It is a Greenland shark. And that number came from its eye. The lens never changes after birth. So they radiocarbon dated it. But here is the part nobody repeats. The real range was two hundred and seventy two, to five hundred and twelve. We do not know how old it is, within two hundred and forty years. It grows less than a centimetre a year, and swims slower than you walk. And nearly all of them are going blind. A parasite clamps onto the eye, and feeds on it. It will keep going for another century. Blind, in the cold, two thousand metres down.
planner_notes: Payoff is the honest range, not the headline number. Numbers go on screen as edit overlays.

characters.name: Greenland shark
characters.description: a large, heavy-bodied shark with a short rounded snout, small dorsal fins set far back, and thick mottled grey-brown skin with pale scars

states.cruising: swimming slowly and steadily, body almost straight, tail sweeping in slow strokes
states.eye_parasite: its eye clouded pale, with a small pale ribbon-like copepod parasite hanging from the eye surface
states.receding: swimming away from the camera, body shrinking into the darkness

locked_attributes: mottled grey-brown skin with pale scars
small dorsal fins set far back
must_avoid: open jaws with rows of teeth

states.in_dish: resting whole in a shallow glass dish
states.sampled: being cut open by fine tweezers and a scalpel under a microscope, exposing its dense inner core
